transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-11
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Liam Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Reyes (Redwood SE), Marco Li (Redwood), Anika Rao (CISO, Guardian), Derek Stone (Head of Platform), Priya Malhotra (Eng Mgr), Ethan Brooks (DevOps)
Artifacts shared: PT final report (https://redwood.test/pt/guardian-2026), remediation spreadsheet (Google Sheet link noted in chat), KMS/HSM integration guide (link)

Summary:
High-level closure of penetration test findings, agreement on immediate patch cadence, discussion of KMS/HSM options for production, audit log retention policy, and SDLC changes to prevent regressions. Decided on a two-week triage sprint and a follow-up technical checkpoint to validate critical fixes.

Topics: SOC 2 implications; RBAC & SSO; audit log retention and tamper-proofing; encryption at rest/in transit (KMS/HSM options); patch cadence and emergency patch windows; secure SDLC/scan automation; proof-of-fix validation.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Liam: Okay everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about an hour, we'll run through the pen test closure items, Sofia and Marco will cover the technical bits, then we can align on patch windows and follow ups.
[00:18] Anika: Thanks, Liam. We want to make sure the high risk items are closed before the next release window, and also understand any impacts to our SOC 2 scope.
[00:27] Sofia: Yep, we triaged the report into critical/high/medium. There were three critical findings — one auth token reuse issue, a misconfigured S3 policy exposing staging artifacts, and a dependency RCE vector tied to a native lib.
[00:38] Derek: The S3 thing is weird — staging is supposed to be air-gapped; looks like a deploy pipeline variable pointed to old bucket. We'll need to lock that down and rotate keys.
[00:50] Priya: We already have a jira epic for the deploy pipeline, I'll attach the exact job. Question — is access key rotation required immediately or can we do scoped IAM role changes?
[01:05] Sofia: Scoped role changes are fine short term but rotate creds within 24 hours for the exposed keys. Also audit logs showed repeated calls from that service account last month.
[01:20] Ethan: For HSM/KMS, we're leaning toward AWS KMS with custom key policy, but the pen test notes concern about key access from CI runners.
[01:33] Marco: Right — we recommended moving any decryption operations off CI and into a short-lived credentialed signing service. Also map HSM usage to an HSM-backed KMS (we documented sample config).
[01:48] Anika: On SOC 2, our auditor will want tamper-evident logs; what retention and WORM options do you recommend?
[01:58] Sofia: For SOC 2, 90 days of hot logs and 12 months archived is common. For tamper-evidence enable checksum + signed log shipping to an immutable store (S3 Object Lock / WORM). We can provide an architecture sketch.
[02:16] Priya: Does Redwood provide any built-in log forwarding for audit logs?
[02:22] Liam: Yes, we have a configurable audit log export in the console — you can push to your own S3/GCS, with optional SSE-KMS encryption. We'll share the config snippet.
[02:33] Derek: There was a notation about RBAC misconfig on a service account, can you explain?
[02:39] Sofia: During pen test the team found that a service account had broader roles than needed — e.g., cluster-admin in staging, should be read-only plus patch rights. Principle of least privilege, and add role-boundary checks in CD pipeline.
[02:55] Anika: We'll update the RBAC policy and add periodic reviews. Also want SSO/SAML enforced for admins.
[03:04] Marco: We recommend SAML enforced for all console access. We also flagged sessions without MFA for a small set of users; that's an easy fix in your IdP.
[03:15] Ethan: In terms of patch cadence, what's realistic? We want weekly app patching and monthly infra windows, with emergency hotfixes.
[03:25] Sofia: That sounds fine — prioritize critical CVEs immediately, high within one week, medium in the next sprint. For infra (OS/kernel) coordinate a monthly maintenance window; Redwood can accept a blackout calendar.
[03:39] Priya: The pen test lists CVE-2025-8432 for our web framework. That's in three internal services. Who owns that?
[03:48] Derek: Platform will own runtime upgrades, app teams will validate.
[03:52] Priya: We'll take the app-side work, Derek will schedule infra upgrades.
[04:01] Liam: Quick note on verification — we can run a light smoke re-scan on your private deployment after patches. Marco can queue that.
[04:09] Marco: Yes, I'll coordinate with Ethan to run the smoke checks and replay the failing PoC. We suggested re-running the actual PoC from the report so you can demonstrate fix.
[04:20] Anika: About the dependency RCE — pen test flagged a native lib with no backported fixes. The recommendation was to vendor the lib and apply a patch; is that the best path?
[04:33] Sofia: Vendor or isolate via process boundaries; long term we also recommend SCA (software composition analysis) in CI to catch native deps. Short term vendor or patch backport.
[04:45] Ethan: We can vendor and apply mitigation flags, then schedule upstream tracking.
[04:50] Priya: For SDLC, can we get Redwood's recommended gating rules? We want to block merges that introduce new critical dependencies.
[04:58] Marco: We have a checklist: SCA fail-build threshold for critical, dependency whitelisting for native libs, mandatory PR sign-off from security owner, and automated CVE comments in PRs. We'll share the checklist.
[05:12] Derek: On data residency — production must stay in EU-West for PHI-like data. Any implications for KMS cross-region keys?
[05:21] Sofia: Keep keys region-scoped and avoid cross-region replication for sensitive keys. Use multi-region replicas only for non-PHI if needed. For Redwood private deployments, we can pin the region.
[05:34] Anika: Audit logs — we need a retention policy plus export to our SIEM. Can logs be exported in near real-time?
[05:41] Liam: Yes, you can stream audit events over SQS/Kafka to your SIEM, or use webhook forwarding. We also support batched exports.
[05:51] Priya: There's a medium finding about weak session timeout defaults — what's recommended?
[05:57] Sofia: Reduce admin console session to 15 minutes idle and force re-auth for privileged ops; also log privileged ops to a separate immutable channel.
[06:10] Anika: A bit surprised by a note about token reuse — is that a Redwood SDK issue or ours?
[06:17] Marco: It looks like a shared token primer in a helper lib in your repo that caches tokens globally; if a token refresh race happens you can leak a token. We flagged the pattern and provided code snippet to fix.
[06:30] Ethan: We'll search the repo for that helper.
[06:33] Priya: Regarding proof-of-fix: will you accept screenshots or do you need a re-run of the PoC?
[06:39] Sofia: Re-run of the PoC is preferable. Screenshots are ok for low/medium but critical should be re-tested. Marco will do a scoped re-test for criticals.
[06:52] Liam: Let's go through the criticals quickly — token reuse, S3 exposure, native lib RCE. Any blockers to remediating these by next week?
[07:03] Priya: No blockers, just coordination across app teams; we might need a short maintenance window for the lib vendoring.
[07:12] Derek: We'll prioritize and block out Friday morning for infra work, can Redwood accept a Friday 0300-0600 maintenance?
[07:20] Liam: Yes, that works, please add to the blackout calendar.
[07:26] Anika: A process question — after fixes, do you recommend an internal retest then external pen test retest?
[07:33] Sofia: Internal retest first (we can run the PoC), then external retest for compliance/auditor evidence. External retest timing depends on your compliance window.
[07:44] Priya: Anything specific for SOC 2 evidence?
[07:48] Marco: Collect ticket links, deploy diffs, config changes, and re-test results; auditors prefer a narrative plus artifacts. We'll prepare a package template.
[07:59] Derek: On encryption at rest, will SSE-KMS be acceptable, or do we need HSM-backed keys in FIPS mode?
[08:08] Anika: For PHI-like workloads we prefer HSM-backed keys in FIPS mode.
[08:13] Sofia: Redwood supports bringing-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM-backed KMS; we documented the steps. We also note that some telemetry still touches metadata, so ensure that meta doesn't include PHI.
[08:27] Ethan: About CI secrets — the report flagged ephemeral secret leaking in logs. Is there a Redwood client best practice?
[08:35] Marco: Mask secrets in CI logs, use short-lived tokens and OIDC where possible; avoid printing env vars. We provided a quick grep script to find potential leaks.
[08:47] Priya: We'll run that script across repos.
[08:50] Anika: Any competitive notes we should be aware of? Our procurement asked if similar vendors required any extra work.
[08:56] Liam: CloudAI offers a similar stack but requires more custom work for private deployments; AcmeSecure had faster HSM onboarding but less observability. We can put together a short comparison if helpful.
[09:10] Derek: Let's talk about the patch cadence detail — what SLA should we commit to for criticals?
[09:18] Sofia: Commit to 72-hour turnaround for criticals (identify, patch, verify), high within 7 days, medium within sprint. That's a common enterprise SLA.
[09:28] Priya: 72 hours is doable with 24/7 oncall for criticals. We'll formalize escalation.
[09:36] Marco: We'll also add a checklist to the remediation sheet: PoC, fix, deploy, smoke test, re-run PoC, close ticket.
[09:48] Liam: Anything else on SDLC hardening?
[09:51] Priya: Add SCA gating, automate IaC scanning, and require security owner sign-off.
[09:57] Anika: Also want to document exceptions with business justification, and have quarterly RBAC audits.
[10:06] Derek: For audit logs retention — can Redwood support multi-tenant log partitioning so we can maintain strict separation?
[10:14] Sofia: Yes, we partition logs by tenant ID and support encryption per-tenant using customer KMS.
[10:22] Ethan: On the topic of key rotation — any guidance for rotation frequency?
[10:27] Marco: For HSM keys monthly key rotation for data keys and yearly for master keys is typical; follow NIST guidance. We'll include a rotation schedule template.
[10:38] Priya: Can Redwood produce a compliance artifact for the fixes we make to feed to our SOC auditor?
[10:45] Liam: Yes, we'll compile a remediation bundle with test outputs, config diffs, and notes for auditors.
[10:52] Anika: Final thing — are you able to run an automated retest that simulates an external attacker without using our infra for PoC?
[10:59] Sofia: We can run blackbox checks from Redwood-managed infra as a verification step, but for final compliance you may want the external vendor retest. We can coordinate both.
[11:12] Marco: Okay wrapping up — I'll assign the re-tests and post links to the outcomes.
[11:18] Liam: Great, we'll shoot the final PT spreadsheet and remediation tracker to the group after the call.
[11:24] Anika: Thanks everyone, we'll prioritize the fixes and get back to you with the maintenance windows.
[11:30] Liam: Next check-in — two weeks from today, same time, to review PoC re-tests and patch progress.

Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: Automatic transcription had a few mis-heards — 'KV cache' appears as 'KV cash' in spots, SAMEL instead of SAML in one line. Names occasionally split (e.g., 'Priya Mal hotra').
